questions.stem: Ultrafiltration of blood in the kidney takes place in the
questions.explanation: Blood enters the glomerulus through a wide arteriole and leaves through a narrower one, which raises the pressure and forces small molecules out through the capillary wall into the Bowmans capsule. Blood cells and plasma proteins are too large to pass and remain in the blood.

distractorRationale.b: The loop of Henle creates the salt gradient used to conserve water
distractorRationale.c: The collecting duct carries out the final water reabsorption under ADH control
distractorRationale.d: The ureter merely conveys finished urine to the bladder

questions.stem: Which substance present in the glomerular filtrate is normally completely reabsorbed before the urine leaves the kidney?
questions.explanation: Glucose is far too valuable to waste, so carrier proteins in the proximal convoluted tubule return every molecule of it to the blood by active transport. Urine from a healthy person therefore contains no glucose, and finding glucose there is a standard test for diabetes mellitus.

distractorRationale.a: Urea is a waste product and is deliberately left in the filtrate
distractorRationale.c: Much water is reabsorbed but never all of it, since some is needed to carry the urea away
distractorRationale.d: Only the salts the body needs are reabsorbed; the excess is excreted

questions.stem: Which components of blood are NOT found in the glomerular filtrate of a healthy kidney?

options.text: Red blood cells and plasma proteins

questions.explanation: Ultrafiltration works like a sieve based on molecular size. Blood cells and plasma proteins are far too large to pass through the capillary wall and the basement membrane, so they stay in the blood, while all the small molecules are forced through.

distractorRationale.a: Water and mineral salts are small and pass into the filtrate freely
distractorRationale.c: Both urea and glucose are small molecules that enter the filtrate, though glucose is later reabsorbed
distractorRationale.d: Amino acids and vitamins pass into the filtrate and are then reabsorbed

questions.stem: An increase in the secretion of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) results in

options.text: a large volume of dilute urine
a small volume of concentrated urine

questions.explanation: ADH makes the walls of the collecting ducts more permeable to water, so more water is reabsorbed into the blood as the filtrate passes through the salty medulla. Less water therefore leaves the body, and the urine that is produced is small in volume and dark.

distractorRationale.a: This is the result of low ADH, when the collecting ducts stay relatively impermeable
distractorRationale.c: Glucose in urine indicates diabetes mellitus, which involves insulin rather than ADH
distractorRationale.d: Protein in urine indicates damage to the filtering membrane

questions.stem: A farmer works all afternoon in the hot sun and sweats heavily without drinking. Which sequence describes his body's response?

options.text: Blood becomes more dilute, less ADH is released, and much dilute urine is produced
Blood becomes more concentrated, more ADH is released, and a small volume of concentrated urine is produced
Blood glucose falls, insulin is released, and glycogen is stored
Blood becomes more concentrated, ADH secretion stops, and water loss increases

questions.explanation: Sweating removes water and leaves the blood more concentrated. The hypothalamus detects the change and the pituitary releases more ADH, which raises the permeability of the collecting ducts so water is reabsorbed. The volume of urine falls, conserving water, and blood concentration returns towards normal.

distractorRationale.a: Sweating concentrates rather than dilutes the blood
distractorRationale.c: Insulin regulates glucose, not water balance
distractorRationale.d: Stopping ADH would increase water loss and worsen the dehydration; the response must cancel the change, not amplify it

questions.stem: When a person becomes too hot, which pair of responses helps to lower body temperature?

options.text: Increased sweating and vasodilation of skin arterioles
Erection of body hair and reduced sweating

questions.explanation: Evaporating sweat absorbs latent heat from the skin, and vasodilation brings more warm blood close to the surface so that heat is lost by radiation and conduction. Both responses increase the rate of heat loss.

distractorRationale.a: Shivering generates heat and vasoconstriction retains it, which are cold responses
distractorRationale.c: Erect hair traps insulating air and reduced sweating conserves heat
distractorRationale.d: Faster respiration would generate more heat, and vasoconstriction would trap it

questions.stem: Which hormone lowers blood glucose by causing the liver to convert glucose into glycogen?
questions.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas when blood glucose rises after a meal. It increases glucose uptake by cells and stimulates the liver to store the surplus as glycogen, so blood glucose falls back to normal.

distractorRationale.a: Glucagon does the opposite, converting glycogen back to glucose when blood sugar is low
distractorRationale.c: Adrenaline raises blood glucose as part of the response to fright or stress
distractorRationale.d: ADH regulates water reabsorption, not glucose

questions.stem: The presence of glucose in a person's urine is normal and shows that the kidney is filtering efficiently.
questions.explanation: False. Although glucose does enter the filtrate, a healthy proximal tubule reabsorbs all of it by active transport. Glucose in urine means the blood glucose was so high that the carriers were saturated, which is the classic sign of diabetes mellitus.

questions.stem: Homeostatic control in the body is described as negative feedback because the

options.text: response counteracts the original change and restores the normal level
body ignores small changes in the internal environment
hormones involved always reduce the rate of reactions

questions.explanation: In negative feedback, a departure from the set point triggers a response in the opposite direction. Rising blood glucose triggers insulin, which lowers it; a concentrated blood triggers ADH, which dilutes it. The corrective response then shuts down as the normal level is restored.

distractorRationale.a: Reinforcing a change is positive feedback, which would drive the system out of control
distractorRationale.c: Homeostatic systems are sensitive to small deviations, which is why levels stay narrow
distractorRationale.d: Some homeostatic hormones, such as glucagon and adrenaline, increase rates of reaction

questions.stem: Describe how urine is formed in a nephron, naming the two main processes involved. Explain what happens to the volume and concentration of urine when a person drinks two litres of water quickly.
markingGuide: Ultrafiltration: blood in the glomerulus is under high pressure because the outgoing arteriole is narrower than the incoming one, forcing water, glucose, amino acids, salts and urea into the Bowmans capsule while blood cells and plasma proteins remain in the blood (4 marks)

Selective reabsorption: all glucose and amino acids are reabsorbed by active transport in the proximal convoluted tubule, along with most mineral salts and much water by osmosis, leaving urea behind (4 marks)
Water conservation: the loop of Henle makes the medulla salty so water can be drawn out of the collecting duct by osmosis (1 mark)
Effect of drinking: the blood becomes more dilute, so the hypothalamus detects the fall in concentration and the pituitary releases less ADH (2 marks)

Consequence: the collecting ducts become less permeable to water, less water is reabsorbed, and a large volume of pale dilute urine is produced until the blood concentration returns to normal (2 marks)
questions.explanation: Urine formation must be presented as filtration followed by selective recovery, with the emphasis on why plasma proteins stay behind and why glucose does not. For the drinking scenario, the chain to trace is dilute blood, less ADH, less permeable collecting ducts, and therefore a large volume of dilute urine.
